title: Which parts make up each of these four expressions?
description: Four expressions are written as sums, their parts are listed and their values are found. Keeko doubts the list and splits a times part into two numbers.
teaching_notes: One idea: only plus signs split an expression into terms, and a taking away becomes adding the negative. Watch for children who split at a times sign.

source: Write each as a sum of terms and list the terms: (a) 5 + 6 × 3 (b) 4 + 15 − 9 (c) 23 − 2 × 4 + 16 (d) 28 + 19 − 8.
video_script.why: The child practises splitting expressions into terms and finding their values.
video_script.substitution: Change each taking away into adding the negative, split at the plus signs, and add.
video_script.anchor: Four expressions to split into parts
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko splits the first expression at the times sign as well as the plus sign, so six times three becomes two separate parts.
video_script.payoff_line: The values are twenty three, ten, thirty one and thirty nine

final_answer.spoken: the values are twenty three, ten, thirty one and thirty nine

never_show: 6 and 3 listed as two separate terms of the first expression
video_script.design: One idea: split at plus signs after changing each taking away into adding the negative. Assumes adding integers. Wrong idea: a times sign also splits the expression. The four expressions stay on the board all video.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; four expressions listed: (a) 5 + 6 × 3 (b) 4 + 15 − 9 (c) 23 − 2 × 4 + 16 (d) 28 + 19 − 8

marks.book: the title card arrives: From your book
marks.ask: the four expressions appear and each is cut by thin lines into parts

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Four expressions are given. How do we write each as a sum, and which parts does each have?

beats.on_screen: the four expressions stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: 12 + 7 split at the plus sign into 12 and 7; 83 − 14 = 83 + (−14)

marks.def: 12 + 7 splits at the plus sign into two parts

narration: <bookmark mark='def'/>An expression splits into parts at its plus signs.
<bookmark mark='change'/>Before that, every taking away is changed into adding the negative number.
<bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four expressions, each with plus signs, minus signs or times signs.

beats.on_screen: To find: each as a sum, its parts, and its value

marks.find: the words sum, parts and value are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write each as a sum, list its parts, and find its value.

marks.one: the first expression is split at its plus sign

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, the first expression. It splits at its one plus sign, so the parts are five and six times three. <bookmark mark='nopl'/>Six times three has no plus sign, so it is one part.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>Six times three is eighteen, and five plus eighteen is twenty three.

marks.two: the second expression is rewritten and its parts are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='two'/>Step two, the second expression. Taking away nine becomes adding negative nine, so the parts are four, fifteen and negative nine.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Four plus fifteen is nineteen, and nineteen plus negative nine is ten.

marks.three: the third expression is rewritten and its parts are marked
marks.add: the parts are added two at a time

narration: <bookmark mark='three'/>Step three, the third expression. Taking away two times four is the same as adding negative two times four.
<bookmark mark='mult'/>The parts are twenty three, negative two times four, and sixteen. Two times four is eight.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Twenty three plus negative eight is fifteen, and fifteen plus sixteen is thirty one.

marks.four: the last expression is rewritten and its parts are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step four, the last expression. Taking away eight becomes adding negative eight, so the parts are twenty eight, nineteen and negative eight.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Twenty eight plus nineteen is forty seven, and forty seven plus negative eight is thirty nine.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>The values are twenty three, ten, thirty one and thirty nine.
<bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows: parts 5, 6, 3; beside it 5 + 6 × 3 with 6 × 3 kept together; the bubble is struck through in the warning colour

marks.fix: 6 × 3 glows as one part and the bubble is struck through

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks the parts of the first expression are five, six and three.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But six times three has no plus sign, so it stays together as one part.
